reviews.t: Not a mirror at all, just silver
reviews.x: It's definitely not a mirror effect. I've painted my nails with gel many times and I followed their directions to the letter. It has a mirror effect that goes away when you apply the top coat. If you remove that step and don't use a top coat, it rubs off completely within hours.  If you follow the steps, it's not a mirror effect at all but a standard silver and something you can buy for $3 somewhere else.

I work in a salon so I know how to do nails. This product peels off. I'm very disappointed in it. I even called the company to ask about application. I feel that the base/topcoat is the problem. It's too slippery to use as base coat so the polish peels in the edges. It's s great topcoat. Very shinny. If you have a solution for this problem please let me know. I didn't send it back because I use the top coat as a clear coat . Keeps my nails strong.

Directions were contradictory and made no sense. Apply the base and top coat just to wipe it off? What residue? It made mention of other products to use in the process that would need to be purchased separately. Sponge, prep, primer, cleanser? It should all come as a kit with proper instructions. It didn't look like chrome. It looked like a dull nickel or aluminum. Waste of money.

claims.text: Most reviewers report the product peels off quickly, often within hours of application.
Many say it does not deliver a true chrome or mirror effect, appearing as plain silver or losing the effect once top coat is applied.
Several reviewers complain about poor or contradictory instructions and unclear application requirements.
A few reviewers note the product looks good before top coat but the shine fades or the effect is lost after sealing.
Some reviewers say the product is easy to apply or works well going on, though lasting power remains an issue.
